# Purpose

SigXTalk's pathway weights are unsigned: they say that a receptor, an intermediate (SSC) and a target gene co-vary,
not whether the target goes up or down in disease. This short, separate analysis adds the missing information. For every
gene that appears in a final pathway (receptor, intermediate or target) it reports the AD-vs-Control change in
microglia.

It needs the result tables of `01_sigxtalk_pipeline.Rmd` (`results/tables/results_AD_full.csv` and
`results/tables/results_Control_full.csv`; the repository already contains them) and the GEO files in `data/`.
The stored output of this analysis is `results/tables/pathway_genes_DE_direction_MG.csv`.

*Why a lighter object is enough.* Seurat's log-normalization is applied to each nucleus independently, so
normalizing only the microglia gives the same values as normalizing all nuclei first. Only microglia are
therefore loaded here, which keeps memory use small.

# Paths and libraries

```{r setup-paths}
stopifnot("Knit this file from inside the analysis/ folder (RStudio does this by default)." =
            basename(getwd()) == "analysis")
repo_root   <- normalizePath("..")
data_dir    <- file.path(repo_root, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "results")
h5_file     <- file.path(data_dir, "GSE174367_snRNA-seq_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
meta_file   <- file.path(data_dir, "GSE174367_snRNA-seq_cell_meta.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(h5_file), file.exists(meta_file))

library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)
```

# Microglia-only Seurat object

The same barcode alignment and the same gene filter (a gene must be detected in at least 3 nuclei) as in the main
pipeline are used, so the number of genes in the object (which the adjusted p-value depends on) matches.

```{r load-microglia}
mat  <- Read10X_h5(h5_file)
meta <- read.csv(meta_file)
mat  <- mat[, colnames(mat) %in% meta$Barcode]
rownames(meta) <- meta$Barcode
meta <- meta[colnames(mat), ]
stopifnot(all(colnames(mat) == rownames(meta)))

mg_cells  <- rownames(meta)[meta$Cell.Type == "MG"]
keep_gene <- Matrix::rowSums(mat > 0) >= 3          # same rule as CreateSeuratObject(min.cells = 3)
mg_only   <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = mat[keep_gene, mg_cells], meta.data = meta[mg_cells, ],
                                min.features = 200)
rm(mat); gc()

mg_only <- NormalizeData(mg_only)
Idents(mg_only) <- mg_only$Diagnosis
table(Idents(mg_only))
```

# Differential expression for the pathway genes

All genes of the final pathways are tested with **no filtering** (`logfc.threshold = 0`, `min.pct = 0`), so that none is
dropped. A positive `avg_log2FC` means higher in AD. `pct.1` and `pct.2` are the fractions of AD and Control
microglia in which the gene is detected.

```{r de-direction}
res_ad <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "tables", "results_AD_full.csv"))
res_ct <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "tables", "results_Control_full.csv"))
pathway_genes <- unique(c(res_ad$Receptor, res_ad$SSC, res_ad$Target,
                          res_ct$Receptor, res_ct$SSC, res_ct$Target))

de <- FindMarkers(mg_only, ident.1 = "AD", ident.2 = "Control", features = pathway_genes,
                  logfc.threshold = 0, min.pct = 0)
de$gene <- rownames(de)

is_in <- function(g, col) g %in% c(res_ad[[col]], res_ct[[col]])
de$role <- sapply(de$gene, function(g)
  paste(c(if (is_in(g, "Receptor")) "receptor",
          if (is_in(g, "SSC"))      "SSC",
          if (is_in(g, "Target"))   "target"), collapse = "/"))
de$direction <- ifelse(de$avg_log2FC > 0, "up in AD", "down in AD")

out <- de[order(de$role, -de$avg_log2FC),
          c("gene", "role", "avg_log2FC", "pct.1", "pct.2", "p_val_adj", "direction")]
write.csv(out, file.path(results_dir, "tables", "pathway_genes_DE_direction_MG.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
out
```

# How to read this

* **Targets** were chosen as AD-vs-Control DE genes, so most are significant; the useful information is their direction.
* **Receptors and intermediates** were *not* selected by DE, so a significant change here is informative and a
  non-significant one is too (for example, the AD-specific receptor MRC1 is not significantly changed).
* **Mixed signs are expected.** The pathway weights are unsigned, so a route can link a gene that goes up to one that goes down.
* The p-values are computed on individual nuclei, which are not independent (nuclei from one donor are correlated). They are
  optimistic. The direction and size of `avg_log2FC` are the more reliable parts of this table. A donor-level
  (pseudobulk) test would be the stricter analysis.
